result:
**Verdict: PASS** for DG1 round 9 on candidate `sha256:05915c32…91babd` (source commit `273d21f`). I found no new problems and verified both fixes assigned to me (F-DG1-213 and F-DG1-129). One check couldn't run here and is marked BLOCKED (below).

**Candidate.** My HEAD at start was `07f1a54`, not the named source commit. That commit only adds assignments, the candidate manifest and `stages.json`, and the candidate ID recomputes the same in the repo and in a full disposable clone. During my run the runner auto-committed the domain reviewer's record (HEAD moved to `39cfc4e`). I didn't open it, and the candidate ID didn't change.

**Checks (all in a disposable clone at `273d21f`):**

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Typecheck, build, lint, OpenAPI lint, no-CDN, format, contrast | all exit 0; OpenAPI has 33 operations |
| Unit tests | 294/294; architecture suite 101/101 |
| Integration on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16, run twice | 200/200 both times; migrations 0001–0008 applied; no 57P01 in either server log (F-DG1-009 holds) |
| Audit log tamper probe | UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE rejected for superuser, owner and app role |
| API contract tests | 9/9, including `getBrandingTokens` |
| Browser tests (Chromium, one worker) | 22/22 in English and Arabic, including the business-unit Lead create → Edit/Archive without a reload (F-DG1-210 holds) |
| Acceptance suites A12, A13, A14, A18, A20 | all pass |
| Gate validators (register, pipeline, reconcile) | all pass |
| The 12 assigned requirements | all marked done, with every cited evidence file present |

**F-DG1-213 / F-DG1-129 (now CLOSED_VERIFIED).** The fix replaces the old block-lists of dangerous Node built-ins and `process` members with allow-lists that deny everything else by default.
- **My own probe** passes 34/34. It checks every built-in (72) and every `process` member (120) of the running Node against my own copy of the safe set: nothing dangerous is allowed and nothing safe is denied. It also covers 23 ways of disguising the calls (all caught) and 6 normal uses (all clean).
- **Round-8 probe replay:** my round-8 probe, which documented the gap, now fails on all three cases. That shows the route is closed.
- **Negative controls:** with the old version of the checker, the `kill` and `_debugProcess` routes slip through again. A real file using them, placed among the API modules, turns the check red; once it is removed the check is green again.
- **Test-only change:** the change touches only the two architecture test files. The checker isn't part of the build, and real module code uses only allowed built-ins, so nothing legitimate is blocked.

**F-DG1-212.** No regression: the installer log cited for REQ-DLV-042 is unchanged, still 14 passed and 0 failed.

**BLOCKED, not affecting the verdict.** Re-running the installer sandbox suite gives 13/14. The failing case (AC-1 "effect") has to fetch from the npm registry, and this sandbox has no network (connection refused). The same case run offline through the unchanged installer passes.

**Observations (not findings).** The allow-list also blocks harmless members such as `process.pid`, `process.cwd` and `node:path/posix`. No module uses them today, so this is intended default-deny behaviour rather than a regression. The checker is a static code check, not a runtime control. Node itself can still start its debugger through these calls; the check only stops module code from using them. F-DG1-010 belongs to the domain reviewer, so I didn't verify it.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG1/round-9/qa-verifier.json` — the review record; the validator reports it as current
- `reviews/DG1/round-9/qa-verifier.verifications.json`
- `reviews/DG1/round-9/qa-verifier.md`
- `test-evidence/DG1/qa/round-9/` — logs
- `test-evidence/DG1/qa/tests/dg1-r9-default-deny-probe.test.ts` — the new probe

The disposable clones have been removed.
